event: Day 43: Wren walks the basin path south on limestone that has learned her gait.
The Vael runs warm beneath her boots; the ground feels familiar.
She passes the Eye's basin without stopping; the bond confirms it is still transmitting SSE.
The circuit is running; she is not its endpoint.
Two hours out she steps over the corruption boundary into silence.
No Vael, no insects, no living bond-awareness: the limestone underfoot carries nothing.
At midday Hearthstone appears: the great ghost-elm ring with its raised root ridges.
Drainage grid, autumn terraces, open clearing; the Greenwater runs lower, quieter.
At the ring gap a resonance rises and meets the Vael in her like two tuned strings.
The bedrock here carries the Vael at full strength, the same as at Varethen.
She lays her palm on the ghost-elm gate post and opens Detail Notation.
A discovery: the Vael does not attenuate; the formation is one resonant body. +67 XP, 2433.

changes.note: Discovery: Vael full-strength propagation at Hearthstone

event: She crosses the ring gap to the central foundation.
Her seven Detail Notation marks from Day 27 are still in the stone.
The first mark holds her Day 27 reading: dense, more present, Apprentice-level, no Vael.
Read now at Journeyman with the Vael, the reinforcement radiates down into the bedrock.
She lets the ten-minute Detail Notation run.
At minute four the bedrock below responds, not to her but to the Eye's transmission.
The signal goes deeper, past the builders' work, into something already there before them.
Hearthstone is a relay, passing the Eye's signal toward a depth her bond cannot follow.
A discovery confirms the signal relay at depth: +100 XP, 2533 / 2573.
She sits a long time with her hand on the foundation, the Greenwater quiet on three sides.
The builders did not build the one thing; they built over it, settling its nodes to take part.
The corruption interrupted the human part, not what lies below.
In the afternoon she reads the other six marks; the well is unchanged and clean.
The drainage grid has more autumn debris, but the limestone and watershed design are sound.
Brecca's interlocking corner now shows pressed intention in its load-bearing stones.
Theron's dry-stack retaining wall shows no subsidence in three hundred years.
The worn market street has no reinforcement: walked on, not worked.
The river gate posts were dressed to shed water: practical, not intentional.
A discovery: the builders pressed the bones, not the skin. +40 XP, 2573 / 2573.

changes.note: Discovery: Detail Notation comparative reading, Hearthstone

event: LEVEL UP: Wren reaches Level 6, with 6 attribute points and a free skill point.

changes.note: Level 6 reached on the Hearthstone comparative reading

event: Next threshold: 3200, 627 XP away.
She renews five marks for thirty days and lets the river gate and market street expire.
Eating dried fruit on the clearing's sheltered east side, a question comes: what are you waiting for?
On Day 27 she chose seeing without holding; she knows more now.
Her Hearth Slot has been empty since the threshold stone opened it.
The Hearth Slot is for home; the threshold stone is where she returns each morning.
Hearthstone is not home, she tells herself clearly: it is a relay node.
The question becomes what she will bring back; she has enough.
She watches the Greenwater catch the afternoon light and resolves to return when she knows more.
She sets out north; the return takes a day and a half.
The first night she camps in a limestone alcove three hours north of Hearthstone.
Both observed intervals were 18 days: pulse two on Day 36, pulse three due Day 54.
Two points are not a pattern; the third pulse will be the test.
If it comes on Day 54 the drift is stable; if later, the drift is growing.
A growing drift is something every settlement in the basin would need to know.
She holds the question in the dark, with a surveyor's attention, not fear.
On the morning of Day 45 she packs camp and walks north.
In late afternoon the settlement appears, the threshold stone felt before it is seen.
Theron looks up from the channel, Hadley lifts a hand, Brecca turns from the wall.
She sets down her pack: 'The foundation is a relay. The builders did not make the system. They joined it.'
Theron is quiet, turning his trowel over.
She explains the pulse test: nine days, and if Day 54 passes without it, the drift is growing.
'I wanted to tell you before the pulse, so you know what to watch for.'
Hadley opens his journal to a new page: nine days to watch.
